kurz: How to determine the figure at which your wealth is enough, and what to put in writing about it in advance.

bloecke.md:
For nineteen modules, the subject was methods: diversifying, cutting costs, putting taxes in order and staying invested during declines. None of these methods answers the question of what the money is for. Without a target, every return seems too low, and every risk can be justified somehow. The comparison with others is then also unwinnable from the outset.

It is said of the writer Joseph Heller that, at a hedge fund manager's party, someone pointed out to him that the host earned more in a single day than Heller had earned with his most successful book over its entire history. John Bogle made Heller's answer the title of a book.

bloecke.text: I have something he will never have: enough.
bloecke.quelle: Joseph Heller, quoted in John C. Bogle, “Enough.” (2008)

bloecke.md:
That sounds like doing without, but the opposite is meant. It is about a figure beyond which additional euros hardly change everyday life any more, whereas additional risk very much does. If this figure is missing, a comparison inevitably takes its place, and a comparison has no end point.

## The target figure as a difference

Enough refers to the part of your needs that no other source covers, and not to the wealth you would like to have. The first deduction can be found in the annual pension statement (Renteninformation), which Deutsche Rentenversicherung (German statutory pension insurance) sends out each year under Section 109 SGB VI (Social Code Book VI, pension insurance) to insured persons aged 27 and over with at least five years of contributions. This figure is a gross amount. For a pension starting in 2026, 84% of the pension is taxable (Section 22 no. 1 sentence 3 letter a double letter aa EStG, Income Tax Act; the share rises by 0.5 points with each new cohort of pensioners and reaches 100% in 2058). Pensioners with compulsory insurance also pay health and long-term care insurance contributions on it (Section 228 SGB V, Social Code Book V, health insurance). Company pensions, rental income and a private pension insurance policy come on top of this. Only the amount still missing after that is the portfolio's job.

bloecke.unter: Model household, all amounts net per month. The two middle bars have already been earned and require no capital. Only the last bar needs to be financed.

schritte.name: Gap to be covered by the portfolio

bloecke.md: €1,100 net a month is €13,200 a year. This part of the calculation is simple. It becomes more difficult because a withdrawal from the portfolio is not a salary. Selling fund units gives rise to investment income (Investmenterträge) under Section 20(1) no. 3 EStG in conjunction with Section 16 InvStG (Investment Tax Act). Only the gain portion of the units sold is taxable. For an equity fund with an equity participation ratio (Kapitalbeteiligungsquote) of more than 50% (Section 2(6) InvStG), 30% of this remains tax-free under Section 20(1) InvStG. The saver's allowance (Sparerpauschbetrag) of €1,000, or €2,000 for joint assessment, is deducted from the remainder (Section 20(9) EStG). The remaining amount is subject to 25% flat-rate withholding tax (Abgeltungsteuer) under Section 32d(1) EStG plus a 5.5% solidarity surcharge, 26.375% in total.

bloecke.titel: Composition of a gross withdrawal of €26,150
bloecke.unter: Illustrative calculation for an equity fund portfolio with a 50% gain portion, one saver's allowance and no church tax. The tax rate on the withdrawal is far below 26.375%, because half of it is a return of your own capital and the partial exemption and the allowance are also deducted from the gain.

teile.name: Flat-rate withholding tax and solidarity surcharge

bloecke.titel: Capital required for a net target

bloecke.md:
The effective rate rises with the withdrawal because the allowance is a fixed amount and is spread over more and more income. The 3.5% is an assumption and not a fixed value. For German investors, a lower rate is the more appropriate assumption because of tax, costs and a possible period of weakness right at the start. Planning with 3.0% requires around one sixth more capital.

Two rules reduce tax in retirement further. With a low taxable income, the most-favourable assessment (Günstigerprüfung) under Section 32d(6) EStG means that capital income is taxed at the personal rate if this is below 25%. Applying for it in the tax return costs nothing, because the tax office only applies the more favourable option. People who are not expected to pay any tax at all can apply for a [[Non-assessment certificate (Nichtveranlagungsbescheinigung)|non-assessment certificate (Nichtveranlagungsbescheinigung)]] under Section 44a(2) EStG and present it to the bank. Then nothing is withheld from the outset.

## Measuring wealth in months

Euros are a poor unit of measurement for financial freedom, because they say nothing about the fixed costs that have to be paid out of wealth. The [[Coverage period|coverage period]] is better suited, that is, liquid assets divided by monthly fixed costs. It indicates how long a household can keep going without income and without having to do anything unwise. This is the figure that matters in an emergency.

This results in an asymmetry that is not visible in euros. The savings side has a linear effect, the spending side does not. Lower fixed costs do not increase the numerator, but they reduce the denominator and at the same time the target figure from the table above.

bloecke.titel: Coverage period of €100,000 at different fixed costs
bloecke.unter: Monthly fixed costs on the x-axis, calculated without return or inflation. The first €600 less a month (from €4,200 to €3,600) brings only around four months of leeway, the last 600 (from €2,400 to €1,800) almost 14. The relationship is therefore not linear.

bloecke.md: Measuring wealth in euros leads to comparison with others; measuring wealth in months leads to comparison with your own life. Only the second figure answers a question that arises in everyday life.

## Comparison with others

Charlie Munger lists envy as No. 8 of his misjudgement tendencies and the contrast-misreaction tendency as No. 16. Both are based on the fact that people judge relative to a reference value and not in absolute terms. Together they make the neighbour's return a particularly unsuitable yardstick, because this figure contains neither his risk nor his losses nor the size of his stake. In addition, the comparison is selective, because hardly anyone among your acquaintances talks about a position that has halved.

The cost of this restlessness becomes measurable in the gap between fund return and investor return. In “Mind the Gap 2026”, Morningstar puts it at 1.2 percentage points a year for the decade to the end of 2025. The funds returned 9.9%, the average dollar invested 8.7%. The difference arose solely from the timing and size of purchases and sales. The size of this gap is disputed, however. In the Financial Analysts Journal in 2026, Fulkerson, Jordan, Riley and Yan consider the damage to be much smaller. But nobody disputes that investors on average do worse than their funds.

Once the target figure has been reached, benefit and harm are no longer symmetrical. A gain of 30% hardly changes your standard of living; a loss of 50% postpones retirement by years. Nevertheless, people in this situation resort to leverage, concentration or securities-backed loans. In doing so, they risk wealth that they have and need for gains that they do not need. The cause is rarely greed in the moral sense; usually a target value is missing.

## Money, consumption and satisfaction

How much money makes people more satisfied is less well documented than the frequently quoted figure suggests. In 2010, Kahneman and Deaton found that daily emotional well-being in the USA only rose with household income up to around $75,000 a year. In 2021, Killingsworth contradicted this with real-time data. A joint follow-up study by both camps resolved the dispute in 2023. According to it, well-being continues to rise above this income for most people and only levels off for an unhappier minority. None of these figures can be transferred directly to German conditions.

Regardless of this, the difference between things and room for manoeuvre remains. A higher standard of consumption has to be financed permanently and ties up capital permanently. Room for manoeuvre, on the other hand, becomes more valuable with every year, because it helps in the situations in which plans no longer work out. Moreover, only costs and needs can be reliably controlled, not the markets. Over 30 years, €10,000 grows to around €72,000 at 7% gross and 0.2% ongoing charges, but only to around €49,800 at 1.5% ongoing charges.

## The investment mission statement in ten sentences

An [[Investment mission statement|investment mission statement]] is a single page that is written in calm times and applies in turbulent ones. Unlike a resolution, it is a precommitment and answers questions before they are asked under pressure. The following ten sentences are fill-in-the-blank texts and not a recommendation.

schritte.text: This money serves … and is not there to impress or outdo anyone.
My enough is … euros net a month. After deducting secure income, a gap of … euros remains, which corresponds to a portfolio of around … euros.
I want to reach this figure by … and for this I assume savings of … euros a month.
My portfolio consists of …; the emergency fund of … months' expenses is held in the instant-access savings account and is not part of the investment.
As a matter of principle, I do not buy the following, regardless of how these products have performed over the last twelve months: …
The ongoing charges of my portfolio stay below …% a year; anything above that must be justified in writing.
If my portfolio falls by 30%, I will do the following: … Selling is not part of it.
I measure myself against my own target figure and against …, not against the returns of acquaintances or annual rankings.
When I reach the target figure, I will reduce the risk to … and not increase it in order to have more faster.
I only change this sheet on … of each year and never within 30 days of a price movement of more than 10%.

bloecke.md: The benefit arises less when writing than when rereading later. This matters above all in three situations: in a decline of 30%, for which sentence 7 already contains a rule; with a product offer with high ongoing charges, on which sentence 6 decides without further discussion; and when someone tells you about doubling their money, because that is what sentence 8 is for. A file and a date are enough. An amended sentence with the date next to it is more valuable than a neatly rewritten sheet.

This happens more often than you might think. Reasons can be an inheritance, a severance payment, a long bull market or needs that are lower than assumed. Three consequences can then be justified objectively: reducing the equity allocation to the level that reliably covers the gap; reducing working hours instead of increasing capital that no longer serves any purpose; or raising the target figure deliberately and in writing because needs have genuinely changed, for example due to children, care or a move. What cannot be justified is shifting the figure upwards without an explicit decision, merely because it has been reached.

mitnehmen: Enough is the difference between your needs and the income that flows anyway, and only this remainder has to come from capital.
Because of tax, €2,000 net a month requires a gross withdrawal of around €26,150 a year and, at a withdrawal percentage of 3.5%, a portfolio of around €747,000.

In the model, the effective tax rate on a withdrawal is around 8% and thus far below 26.375%, because half of the withdrawal is a return of your own capital and the partial exemption and allowance are also deducted from the gain.
Measured in months of coverage period, wealth answers a question that arises in your own life; measured in euros, it only answers the comparison with others.
An investment mission statement works because it was written before the situation and contains a revision rule; good wording does not matter.

begriffe.text: Written advance commitment, in a few sentences, on the purpose of the money, target figure, allocation, exclusion criteria, cost limit and behaviour in a decline, supplemented by a rule on when the document may be changed.
Liquid assets divided by monthly fixed costs. The coverage period measures wealth in months without income rather than in euros and shows how much room for manoeuvre a sum provides.

Share of the portfolio value that is withdrawn each year. The target figure is the annual requirement divided by the percentage. At 3.5%, it corresponds to 28.6 times the annual requirement, at 3.0% to 33.3 times.

Certificate from the tax office under Section 44a(2) EStG for persons whose income is expected to remain below the basic tax-free allowance (Grundfreibetrag). The bank then withholds no flat-rate withholding tax from the outset.
